sections.heading: Xenophon's Agesilaus
paragraphs: The English text here is E. C. Marchant's Loeb Classical Library translation, verbatim ("Xenophon in Seven Volumes", vol. 7, Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press; London: William Heinemann Ltd., 1925). Nothing is modernised, paraphrased or silently corrected.

sections.heading: The edition
paragraphs: E. C. Marchant, ed., Xenophontis Opera Omnia, vol. 5 (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1920), an Oxford Classical Text - Greek title "Ἀγησίλαος". The Loeb English translation used here is by E. C. Marchant (vol. 7, 1925).
Structure: chapter, then section (no book level). This edition carries 11 chapter(s), 137 section(s) total in this witness.

sections.heading: Digital source
paragraphs: The machine-readable text is the TEI XML file tlg0032.tlg009.perseus-eng2.xml (CTS urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0032.tlg009.perseus-eng2) from the Perseus Digital Library / OpenGreekAndLatin canonical-greekLit repository. It was fetched once (cached at scripts/import-xenophon/raw/) and is bundled with the app; nothing is loaded from the network at runtime.

sections.heading: How it was imported
paragraphs:
The importer walks the flat sequence of chapter
s (no book wrapper in this source). Each Chapter becomes a leaf Division (`ch-N`) with exactly one Passage, collecting every

under that chapter's section children, in citation-number order, joined with a blank line.

Only transport/editorial scaffolding is removed: entities are decoded, whitespace collapsed, and Unicode normalised to NFC (a no-op for every one of these 14 source files - independently verified 0 code points remapped). markers (always redundant with an immediately-following

start) are dropped as zero-width. Editorial supplements () and corrections (, standalone or the printed half of a / pair) ARE part of what this edition prints as its running text and are kept verbatim; text the editor brackets as suspected spurious or an interpolation () is likewise KEPT, wrapped in square brackets exactly as a critical edition prints editor-bracketed text - NOT excluded (only the unemended half of a pair, and any translator footnote nested inside a , are ever excluded); all logged individually in anomalies.json, full span verbatim. Translator/editorial footnotes (, up to ~1450 in one file) and inline source-attribution labels for embedded quotations (, e.g. "Theognis") are excluded entirely as apparatus, not Xenophon's own words, and counted.

sections.heading: Reference scheme
paragraphs: Citation is by Chapter and Section (e.g. "Agesilaus 1.1"), Xenophon's and this edition's own numbering. This app's schema folds each chapter's sections into one Passage (see "How it was imported"), so Division.ref and Passage.ref are null throughout.

sections.heading: Known gaps & anomalies
paragraphs: Completeness. All 11 chapters and 137 sections of this edition are present and in order.

1 <gap reason="lost"/> manuscript lacuna marker(s) were found; this edition prints no literal rendering at any of them (no "rend" attribute anywhere in this corpus), so nothing is fabricated. Logged individually.
38 translator/editorial footnote(s) (<note>) were excluded entirely as apparatus - never Xenophon's own words.

22 inline source-attribution label(s) (<bibl>, e.g. naming the poet a quoted line traces to) were excluded from the reading text as editorial apparatus - confirmed by direct inspection to be glued onto the surrounding text with no separating whitespace, i.e. never part of Xenophon's own sentence.
